concept.name: Bid-ask footprint
concept.definition: The most common footprint display mode: at every price level inside a bar, two numbers are shown side by side — the volume traded at the bid (seller-initiated) and the volume traded at the ask (buyer-initiated). It exposes where aggressive buying and selling actually occurred within each bar.
concept.intuition: It is the scoreboard of the intra-bar fight, level by level: how much sellers hit bids versus how much buyers lifted offers at each price.
concept.mechanics: Tick data are classified by execution side and aggregated per price level per bar; each cell displays 'bid volume × ask volume' (or vice versa), commonly color-coded by which side dominates, and diagonal bid/ask comparisons are used for imbalance analysis.
concept.failure_modes: Same data-quality dependencies as all bid/ask statistics — misclassified ticks distort the per-level split; at very small tick sizes or fast markets the cells become dense and hard to read without aggregation.
concept.misconceptions: A dominant ask side at a level does not guarantee price will rise from there; it records aggression that has already happened and can mark absorption by passive sellers just as easily as initiative buying.
concept.example: At a resistance level, a footprint cell shows 320 × 1,450 (bid × ask); the trader sees buyers lifted 1,450 contracts at the offer, then watches whether price advances or stalls on that aggression.
